title: Towards Privacy-Preserving and Heterogeneity-aware Split Federated Learning via Probabilistic Masking

problem.claim: Split Federated Learning exposes intermediate activations and model updates to data reconstruction risks while supporting clients with heterogeneous data and system resources.

gap.claim: Existing noise-injection defenses often reduce model performance.

contributions.claim: PM-SFL uses Probabilistic Mask training to add structured randomness without explicit noise.
PM-SFL uses personalized mask learning to tailor submodel structures to each client's local data.
PM-SFL introduces layer-wise knowledge compensation for clients with varying resources under adaptive model splitting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis confirms PM-SFL's privacy protection.
The authors report that experiments on image and wireless sensing tasks show improved accuracy, communication efficiency, and robustness to privacy attacks.
The authors report particularly strong performance under data and system heterogeneity.

narrative_sequence.summary: SFL reduces client-side computation through model partitioning.
Intermediate representations and updates create reconstruction risks, while noise-based defenses can harm performance.
PM-SFL combines probabilistic masking, personalized mask learning, and layer-wise knowledge compensation to address privacy, data heterogeneity, and system heterogeneity.
The authors report theoretical privacy analysis and experimental improvements across image and wireless sensing tasks.

source_observation.claim: Structured randomness is used to mitigate reconstruction risks without explicit noise injection.

interpretation.claim: Privacy mechanisms may seek utility preservation by altering model structure or representations rather than adding conventional noise.

application.claim: When noise injection harms performance, investigate structured masking or representation-level alternatives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when structured masking outperforms noise injection or how its privacy guarantees compare quantitatively.

source_observation.claim: Separate mechanisms address data heterogeneity and system heterogeneity.

interpretation.claim: Federated systems may require distinct adaptations for client-data differences and client-resource differences.

application.claim: Design heterogeneous-client methods with explicit data-personalization and resource-adaptation components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the heterogeneity ranges, client populations, or adaptation costs.

unknowns: Privacy threat model, attack configuration, and quantitative privacy guarantees are unspecified.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical experimental results are unspecified.
Theoretical assumptions and proof details are unspecified.
